name: Restylane Defyne / Lyft / Kysse

lead: Three Restylane gels: Lyft for cheeks and midface, Defyne for lines and contour, Kysse for lips.
Lyft has randomized trials in midface deficit; Defyne and Kysse have less published trial detail in the available literature.

paras: Cross-linked HA gels of differing firmness and particle size add volume and support, then degrade gradually; hyaluronidase can dissolve them.
Typical effects are bruising and swelling; rarely, vascular occlusion. These are prescription devices injected by licensed clinicians.

lead: Restylane Defyne, Restylane Lyft and Restylane Kysse are hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal fillers in the Restylane range made by Galderma, which acquired the original developer Q-Med in 2011 according to Grokipedia. [1] Lyft is a large-gel-particle product for cheeks and midface (and hands); Defyne is a flexible gel for smile lines and facial contouring; Kysse is for lip enhancement and perioral lines. [1]

Randomized trials report effectiveness of Lyft for midface volume deficit and nasolabial folds, and trials have examined jawline, chin and nose uses. [2][3][4][5] In looksmaxxing discussions these products are referred to as options for cheeks, chin, jawline and lips.
infobox: Lyft: cheeks, chin, hands; Defyne: lines/contour; Kysse: lips
Defyne 2016; Lyft hands 2018; Kysse 2020; Lyft chin 2025 [1]

paras: Lyft uses a large-gel-particle HA formulation for volume in the cheeks and midface and, per Grokipedia, was approved for hand augmentation in 2018 and mild-to-moderate chin retrusion in November 2025. [1]

Defyne is described as having flexible gel particles meant to move with facial expression, used for smile lines and shaping; Grokipedia says the FDA approved Defyne in 2016 using Optimal Balance Technology, though that page is internally inconsistent about the technology names. [1]
Kysse is used for lip enhancement and upper perioral lines; Grokipedia reports FDA approval in 2020. [1]

Laboratory studies have measured how HA fillers, including Restylane products, are digested by hyaluronidase. [6][7] A 2024 study compared NASHA and OBT gels for strength and flexibility. [8] A review notes that HA fillers are not interchangeable and have distinct characteristics. [9]

Regulators and reviews list bruising, swelling, infection, allergic reactions and, rarely, vascular occlusion leading to tissue necrosis or blindness as complications of dermal fillers generally. [10]

In a randomized trial subjects with midface deficiency were assigned 3:1 to Lyft or no treatment and effectiveness and safety were evaluated. [2] A randomized evaluator-blinded split-face study in China compared Lyft with Restylane for nasolabial folds over 12 months. [3] A randomized no-treatment-control study evaluated Lyft for shaping the nasal dorsum and radix. [4] A study examined whether skin thickness should guide midface filler choice. [5] A five-step hand rejuvenation technique has also been described. [11]
Registered trials include jawline contouring and definition (n=40, n=140), chin augmentation (n=45; retreatment study recruiting) and cheek augmentation satisfaction (n=60). [12][13][14]

timeline.event: US approval of Restylane Defyne and Refyne (per Grokipedia). [1]
Kysse approved for lips and perioral lines. [1]
